items.title: A proposed order authorizing the Corporation Counsel to enter into and execute a Settlement Order in the following sixteen (16) cases

enrichment.relevance_reason: The item is a legal settlement of sixteen civil lawsuits against the City and does not concern building, financing, regulating, or occupying homes.
enrichment.summary: Proposed order authorizing the Corporation Counsel to execute a Settlement Order in sixteen federal cases captioned against Guevara et al., totaling $260,814,000. The Department of Law is the sponsor.

items.title: An ordinance authorizing the execution of an intergovernmental agreement with the Chicago Board of Education to provide TIF funds for improvements at Harriet Beecher Stowe Elementary School, located at 3444 W. Wabansia Avenue.

enrichment.relevance_reason: The item concerns TIF funds for school improvements at an elementary school, which does not bear on homes, housing construction, financing, or tenant rights.

items.title: An ordinance authorizing the execution of an intergovernmental agreement with the Chicago Board of Education to provide TIF funds for improvements at Suder Montessori Magnet Elementary School, located at 2022 W. Washington Boulevard.

enrichment.relevance_reason: The item concerns TIF funds for school building improvements, which is not about homes, housing finance, or residents' housing rights.

items.title: A substitute ordinance approving the execution of the 66th amending agreement with SomerCor 504, Inc. to increase the amount of grant funds available in various redevelopment project areas, amend the Small Business Improvement Fund (SBIF) program rules, and authorize SomerCor 504, Inc. to continue providing administrative services for the program.

enrichment.relevance_reason: The item concerns the Small Business Improvement Fund, which provides grants to commercial businesses in redevelopment project areas, and does not involve building, financing, preserving, regulating, or taxing homes or tenant rights.

items.title: An ordinance authorizing the execution of a Redevelopment Agreement with BTH Development, NFP to provide Housing and Economic Development Bond (HED) funds for redevelopment of Altgeld Gardens Youth Center project at 13122 S. Ellis Avenue.

enrichment.relevance_reason: The item funds redevelopment of a youth center, a community facility, and the material does not mention any housing units.
enrichment.summary: Ordinance authorizing a Redevelopment Agreement with BTH Development, NFP for up to $7,300,000 in Housing and Economic Development Bond funds to redevelop the Altgeld Gardens Youth Center at 13122 S. Ellis Avenue (10th Ward).

items.title: An ordinance authorizing the execution of a Redevelopment Agreement with North Lawndale Catalyst Initiative, NFP to provide Housing and Economic Development (HED) funds and tax increment financing (TIF) assistance for the Filmore Linen Services project at 920-922 S. Campbell Avenue.

enrichment.relevance_reason: The item funds a linen services commercial/industrial project with HED and TIF assistance, and the material mentions no housing units.
enrichment.summary: Ordinance authorizing a Redevelopment Agreement with North Lawndale Catalyst Initiative, NFP for up to $5,000,000 in HED funds and up to $5,000,000 in TIF assistance for the Filmore Linen Services project at 920-922 S. Campbell Avenue (28th Ward).

items.title: An ordinance authorizing the execution of a Redevelopment Agreement with Hudson Michigan Avenue Owner LLC to provide Housing and Economic Development (HED) funds for the Hudson House project at 2222 S. Michigan Avenue.

enrichment.relevance_reason: The ordinance would commit City HED loan and grant funds to a named housing project, Hudson House, which bears on city financing of housing.
enrichment.summary: Ordinance authorizing a Redevelopment Agreement with Hudson Michigan Avenue Owner LLC for the Hudson House project at 2222 S. Michigan Avenue (3rd Ward). It provides HED funds: up to $5,000,000 as a city loan and up to $10,000,000 as a city grant.

items.title: One (1) proposed order authorizing the payment of various small claims against the City of Chicago.

enrichment.relevance_reason: The item authorizes payment of miscellaneous small claims against the city, which does not concern building, financing, regulating, or protecting homes or tenants' rights.

items.title: One (1) proposed orders denying the payment of various small claims against the City of Chicago.

enrichment.relevance_reason: The item concerns denying payment of miscellaneous small claims against the City and does not bear on homes, housing finance, regulation, or tenant rights.

items.title: Appointment of Vernell Givens as Commissioner of Chicago Housing Authority for a term effective immediately and expiring August 31, 2031.

enrichment.relevance_reason: The item is an appointment of a Chicago Housing Authority commissioner, which bears on governance of the city's public housing agency.
enrichment.summary: The Committee on Housing and Real Estate will consider the appointment of Vernell Givens as a Chicago Housing Authority Commissioner, with a term effective immediately and expiring August 31, 2031.

items.title: Appointment of Mary Gardner as Commissioner of Chicago Housing Authority for a term effective immediately and expiring August 31, 2031.

enrichment.relevance_reason: The item concerns a mayoral appointment to the Chicago Housing Authority board of commissioners, which governs public housing in Chicago.
enrichment.summary: The Committee on Housing and Real Estate will consider the appointment of Mary Gardner as a Commissioner of the Chicago Housing Authority, for a term effective immediately and expiring August 31, 2031.

items.title: Appointment of Hipolito (Paul) Roldan as Commissioner of Chicago Housing Authority

enrichment.relevance_reason: The item concerns appointment of a Chicago Housing Authority commissioner, who helps govern public housing policy and actions.
enrichment.summary: Mayor Brandon Johnson has appointed Hipolito (Paul) Roldan as a Chicago Housing Authority commissioner for a term effective immediately and expiring July 7, 2031. The City Council is asked to give favorable consideration to the appointment.

items.title: Sale of City-owned property at 11414 S Halsted St to Far South CDC under Low-Income Housing Tax Credits program for redevelopment of Morgan Park Commons (repeal and replacement of O2026-0026567 in entirety)

attachments.label: O2026-0029008 Ex C Site Plan and Project Phases
O2026-0029008 Ex B Legal Description of Dev Property

enrichment.relevance_reason: It authorizes sale of City-owned land to a nonprofit developer for a mixed-income housing redevelopment tied to Low-Income Housing Tax Credits and the ARO.
enrichment.summary: Repeals and replaces ordinance O2026-0026567 to authorize selling the City-owned 11414 S Halsted St parcel to Far South CDC for $1.00 per tax parcel, for Morgan Park Commons. Phase 1 would have 70 mixed-income units, 66 of them affordable.

items.title: Sale of City-owned property at 1335 S Springfield Ave to MKB Business Strategies LLC in Trust for Use of Schools

attachments.label: O2026-0029007 Ex B Depiction of Property

enrichment.relevance_reason: The ordinance conveys a former school site to a developer that plans to demolish the existing building and build 13 single-family homes and 13 affordable three-flats.
enrichment.summary: The City Council would accept MKB Business Strategies, LLC's $25,000 bid and convey the Board of Education's 1335 S Springfield Ave school site. MKB plans to demolish the building and build 13 single-family houses and 13 affordable three-flats in two phases. Title reverts if use restrictions are breached.

items.title: Sale of City-owned property at 2830 W Wilcox St, 2860 W Cermak Rd, 5016 S Christiana Ave, 7713 S Dobson St, 5008, 5010, 5012, 5014, 5016 and 5018 S Throop St to various buyers under ChiBlockBuilder

enrichment.relevance_reason: The ordinance sells vacant City-owned lots for deed-restricted community open space and garden projects, not for housing.
enrichment.summary: The City would sell 11 vacant City-owned lots through ChiBlockBuilder at 10% of market value to community buyers for gardens and open space. Each deed restricts the lot to an open space project and requires the buyer to own it at least five years.

items.title: Sale of City-owned property at 1948 W 63rd St to Reynoso Insulation LLC under ChiBlockBuilder

enrichment.relevance_reason: The sale of two vacant city-owned lots is for a commercial parking lot serving an adjacent business, with no housing units involved.
enrichment.summary: Ordinance would sell two vacant City-owned lots at 1948 W. 63rd St. to Reynoso Insulation, LLC for $18,006 through ChiBlockBuilder. The buyer plans a commercial parking lot for its adjacent business; no zoning change and no ARO units.

items.title: Sale of City-owned property at 2054 and 2058 W Warren Blvd to EGP Warren Apartments LLC under ChiBlockBuilder

enrichment.relevance_reason: It is a sale of City-owned land under the ChiBlockBuilder program, which disposes of public land for housing development.
enrichment.summary: Ordinance would authorize the sale of City-owned property at 2054 and 2058 W Warren Blvd to EGP Warren Apartments LLC under ChiBlockBuilder, at the request of the Department of Planning and Development. The filing discloses Neelam Dwivedi as manager and 100% owner.

items.title: Sale of City-owned property at 4927, 4935 and 4937 S Forrestville Ave to TK Palos LLC under ChiBlockBuilder

enrichment.relevance_reason: It approves sale of city-owned vacant land for market-rate residential development through ChiBlockBuilder, a disposition of public land for housing.
enrichment.summary: The City Council would approve the sale of city-owned lots at 4927, 4935 and 4937 S Forrestville Ave to TK Palos LLC through the Department of Planning and Development's ChiBlockBuilder program, for a market-rate project. The sale is as-is, with a deed restriction.

items.title: Sale of City-owned property at 4549 S Indiana Ave to Click Development LLC 4549 Indiana under ChiBlockBuilder

enrichment.relevance_reason: The item authorizes sale of City-owned land at 4549 S Indiana Ave under the ChiBlockBuilder program, which disposes of public land for housing development.
enrichment.summary: Ordinance would authorize the sale of City-owned property at 4549 S Indiana Ave to Click Development LLC 4549 Indiana under ChiBlockBuilder. The Mayor transmitted it at the Planning and Development Commissioner's request; the buyer is owned by Craig Yarbrough.

items.title: Sale of City-owned property at 3729, 3731 and 3733 S Giles Ave to Iron Eagle LLC under ChiBlockBuilder

enrichment.relevance_reason: The item sells three City-owned vacant lots for construction of new residential buildings under the ChiBlockBuilder program.
enrichment.summary: The City would sell three lots at 3729, 3731 and 3733 S Giles Ave in Bronzeville to Iron Eagle LLC for $250,000 under ChiBlockBuilder. The buyer would build three three-story buildings with three 3-bedroom units each, with no ARO units.

items.title: Sale of City-owned property at 1509 E 67th Pl to 1509 E. 67th PL LLC under ChiBlockBuilder

enrichment.relevance_reason: It authorizes sale of vacant City-owned land for market-rate development through the ChiBlockBuilder program, which disposes of public land for housing.
enrichment.summary: The ordinance would sell vacant City-owned property at 1509 E 67th Pl in as-is condition to 1509 E. 67th PL LLC for market-rate development through ChiBlockBuilder, subject to a deed restriction and closing conditions set by the Department of Planning and Development.

items.title: Sale of City-owned property at 4849, 4853 and 4857 W West End Ave to Medlock Development LLC under ChiBlockBuilder

enrichment.relevance_reason: The ordinance would sell City-owned lots to a developer for a 15-unit new construction housing project under the ChiBlockBuilder program.
enrichment.summary: Ordinance authorizing the sale of City-owned lots at 4849, 4853 and 4857 W West End Ave to Medlock Development LLC under ChiBlockBuilder. The applicant's disclosure describes a 15-unit new construction project; the Department of Planning and Development requested it.

items.title: President’s Update

enrichment.relevance_reason: The CLIHTF board oversees Chicago's Low-Income Housing Trust Fund, which subsidizes rental housing for low-income tenants, though this item is only a general president's update.
enrichment.summary: The President's Update is a standing item on the CLIHTF Board of Directors' October 13, 2026 agenda. The material gives no details of its content.

items.title: Reports

enrichment.relevance_reason: The Chicago Low-Income Housing Trust Fund board hears committee reports on rental subsidy allocations, a property ownership change, and a draft 2027 budget for its affordable rental subsidy program.
enrichment.summary: CLIHTF board receives committee reports, including an allocations summary, an ownership change of 6815 N Sheridan from Patricia Johnson to Teko Properties, financial statements through September 30, 2026, and the draft 2027 budget.

items.title: Allocations Summary

enrichment.relevance_reason: The Chicago Low-Income Housing Trust Fund board is receiving its Allocations Committee report on rental subsidy allocations for low-income housing.
enrichment.summary: The CLIHTF Board of Directors will receive an Allocations Summary from the Allocations Committee, chaired by Adonya Little. No allocation amounts, properties, or unit counts are given beyond the agenda title.

items.title: Ownership change of 6815 N Sheridan from Patricia Johnson to Teko Properties

enrichment.relevance_reason: The item concerns an ownership change for a rental property at 6815 N Sheridan, which is handled through the Chicago Low-Income Housing Trust Fund's rental subsidy program.
enrichment.summary: The CLIHTF Board's Allocations Committee report includes an ownership change for 6815 N Sheridan from Patricia Johnson to Teko Properties. The material gives no further details.

items.title: Financial Statements as of September 30, 2026

enrichment.relevance_reason: The Chicago Low-Income Housing Trust Fund, which funds rental subsidies for low-income tenants, will review its financial statements as part of its board's oversight of affordable housing funding.
enrichment.summary: The CLIHTF Board's Finance and Audit Committee, with Treasurer Meredith Muir, will report on the Trust Fund's financial statements as of September 30, 2026. The same meeting includes a draft 2027 budget presentation.

items.title: Presentation of draft 2027 Budget

enrichment.relevance_reason: The Chicago Low-Income Housing Trust Fund's 2027 budget governs funding for its rental subsidy program for low-income renters.
enrichment.summary: The CLIHTF Board's Finance and Audit Committee, with Treasurer Meredith Muir reporting, will present a draft 2027 budget for the Chicago Low-Income Housing Trust Fund. No budget figures are provided in the material.

items.title: Outreach Committee Update provided by Board VP Sam Paler-Ponce

enrichment.relevance_reason: The Chicago Low-Income Housing Trust Fund board is receiving an update on its outreach work, which supports its rental subsidy program for low-income tenants.
enrichment.summary: Board Vice President Sam Paler-Ponce will give an Outreach Committee update at the CLIHTF Board of Directors meeting. The agenda gives no further detail on the update.

items.title: New Business: Tenant Outreach Initiative presented by Marlana Edwards, Director of Program Development and Outreach

enrichment.relevance_reason: The Chicago Low-Income Housing Trust Fund board will hear a Tenant Outreach Initiative, which concerns tenants in subsidized rental housing.
enrichment.summary: The CLIHTF Board of Directors will hear a new-business presentation on a Tenant Outreach Initiative from Marlana Edwards, Director of Program Development and Outreach. The material gives no further detail on the initiative.

items.title: Establishment of Problem Landlord and Housing Court Coordination Task Force to examine and recommend improvements to response to chronic and repeat housing code violations

enrichment.relevance_reason: The resolution creates a task force to examine enforcement of building code violations by problem landlords and coordination with housing and eviction court, bearing on tenant protections and habitability.
enrichment.summary: Resolution sponsored by Ald. Gilbert Villegas (36th) would create a Problem Landlord and Housing Court Coordination Task Force of City Council, Mayor's Office, Buildings, Law and Circuit Court representatives. It would examine repeat building code violations and report recommendations within 180 days of its first meeting.

items.title: Amendment of Municipal Code Section 17-9-0129 allowing lawful cannabis dispensaries to modify to include medical cannabis without triggering Section 17-9-0129.1

enrichment.relevance_reason: The item concerns zoning rules for cannabis dispensaries, a commercial use, and does not involve building, financing, preserving, regulating, taxing, or demolishing homes or tenant rights.

items.title: Amendment of Municipal Code Chapter 17-3 by adding Section 17-3-0600 regarding transient-oriented development (TOD) streets

enrichment.relevance_reason: The ordinance amends the Zoning Ordinance to set TOD street designation, rezoning requirements, design standards, and lower parking caps for residential projects near transit, which affect where and how homes are built.
enrichment.summary: Mayor Johnson, at the Planning and Development Commissioner's request, proposes a new Section 17-3-0600 creating TOD streets. Rezonings along them must go to B or C1 districts with at least 3 FAR, with building design standards. Residential parking near transit is capped at 0.5 spaces per unit.

items.title: Designation of segment of N Western Ave right-of-way on Map Nos. 9-H, 9-I, 11-H, 11-I, 13-H, and 13-I as Transient Oriented Development (TOD) Street and amendment of Municipal Code Section 17-3-0602-F designating portion of N Western Ave as Transient Oriented Development (TOD) Street

attachments.label: TOD Street - Western Avenue - Addison to Ainslie (1)

enrichment.relevance_reason: Designating a stretch of N Western Ave as a TOD street changes zoning rules that govern residential density and parking for development along the corridor.
enrichment.summary: Ordinance by Aldermen Matthew J. Martin (47th) and Andre Vasquez Jr. (40th) designates N Western Ave between W Addison St and W Ainslie St as a Transit Oriented Development (TOD) street and amends Municipal Code Section 17-3-0602-F to list the segment.

items.title: Designation of segment of N Ravenswood Ave right-of-way on Map No. 11-H as Transient Oriented Development (TOD) Street and amendment of Municipal Code Section 17-3-0602-F designating portion of N Ravenswood Ave as Transient Oriented Development Street

attachments.label: TOD Street -  Ravenswood Avenue - Irving Park to Lawrence

enrichment.relevance_reason: TOD street designations in the Chicago Zoning Ordinance change development standards such as parking and density allowances for residential projects along the corridor.
enrichment.summary: Ordinance sponsored by Alderman Matthew J. Martin (47th Ward) would designate N Ravenswood Ave between W Irving Park Rd and W Lawrence Ave as a Transit Oriented Development Street on Map 11-H and amend Section 17-3-0602-F of the Zoning Ordinance.

items.title: Repeal of historical landmark designation for Cortland Bridge

enrichment.relevance_reason: The item repeals a historical landmark designation for a bridge, which does not involve building, financing, preserving, regulating, taxing, or demolishing homes or the rights of residents.

items.title: Historical landmark fee waiver for property at 208 S LaSalle St

attachments.label: Permit Fee Waiver - 208 S LaSalle signed

enrichment.relevance_reason: The item is a landmark permit fee waiver for 208 S. LaSalle St. and nothing in the material mentions homes or residential use.
enrichment.summary: A historical landmark permit fee waiver for the property at 208 S. LaSalle St., applied for by 208 LaSalle Owner, LLC. The attached disclosure statements, filed through The Prime Group, Inc. and RCP Holdings, LLC, give no details on the project.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map Nos. 1-H and 3-H at 1600-1760 W Chicago Ave and 1601-1759 W Chicago Ave

enrichment.relevance_reason: A city-initiated-style rezoning along W Chicago Ave changes B1 neighborhood shopping districts to B3 community shopping districts, which affects what can be built, including residential, on the corridor.
enrichment.summary: Ordinance sponsored by Alderman Daniel La Spata (1st Ward) would rezone parcels along 1600-1760 W Chicago Ave and 1601-1759 W Chicago Ave from B1-2 and B1-3 to B3-2 and B3-3. Several parcels with other existing zoning are excluded.

geography.address: 1600-1760 W Chicago Ave and 1601-1759 W Chicago Ave

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 10-F at 4639-4643 S Wallace St

enrichment.relevance_reason: A rezoning from a B2-3 mixed-use district to RS-3 single-unit detached house district changes the residential development allowed on the site.
enrichment.summary: Ordinance sponsored by Ald. Raymond A. Lopez (15th Ward) would rezone the area at 4639-43 S Wallace Street from B2-3 Neighborhood Mixed-Use District to RS-3 Residential Single Unit (Detached House) District on Map No. 10-F.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 12-F at 5000-5046 S Wells St

enrichment.relevance_reason: The rezoning changes a B1-1 commercial district to RS-3 residential single-unit district, altering what residential and commercial development is allowed on the site.
enrichment.summary: Ordinance would rezone the area bounded by West 50th Street, South Wells Street, a line 125 feet north of West 51st Street, and the alley to the west, from B1-1 Neighborhood Shopping District to RS-3 Residential Single-Unit (Detached House) District. Sponsored by Alderwoman Jeanette B. Taylor, 20th Ward.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 17-H at 1721 W Greenleaf Ave

enrichment.relevance_reason: The rezoning would change a site from an RT-4 residential two-flat/townhouse/multi-unit district to a B3-3 commercial district, which could remove residential zoning capacity.
enrichment.summary: Ordinance sponsored by Ald. Maria Hadden (49th Ward) would rezone the area at 1721 W. Greenleaf Ave from RT-4 Residential Two-Flat, Townhouse and Multi-Unit District to B3-3 Community Shopping District. No project or unit details are provided.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map Nos. 8-F and 10-F at 3800-3958 S State St, 3901-3959 S Dearborn St, 3900-3958 S Dearborn St, 3901-3959 S Federal St, 3900-3946 S Federal St, 2-24 W Pershing Rd, 1-109 W Pershing Rd and 2-52 W 40th St - App No. 23087

enrichment.relevance_reason: The rezoning amends Planned Development 1143 to expand its boundaries, with a Phase II that includes multi-family housing on partly City-owned land and the applicant marking the project as subject to the ARO.
enrichment.summary: P.S. Bronzeville, LLC seeks to rezone RS-3, RT-4 and PD 1143 land near 39th and State to C3-3 and then to an amended Business PD 1143. Phase I is a 70,000 sq ft grocery-anchored mixed-use project; Phase II north of Pershing would include multi-family housing. The applicant marked the project as subject to the ARO.

geography.address: 3800-3958 S State St, 3901-3959 S Dearborn St, 3900-3958 S Dearborn St, 3901-3959 S Federal St, 3900-3946 S Federal St, 2-24 W Pershing Rd, 1-109 W Pershing Rd and 2-52 W 40th St

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No.  4-E at 1608 S Wabash Ave - App No. 23131

enrichment.relevance_reason: The rezoning from DX-5 to DS-3 supports storing and selling construction materials with zero dwelling units, so it does not add or remove homes.
enrichment.summary: 1608 S Wabash Avenue, LLC seeks to rezone 1608 S. Wabash Ave. from DX-5 to DS-3 to store construction materials (insulation, metal framing, wall board) for sale and delivery. The proposal includes no dwelling units.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 10-E at 3927-3933 S Martin Luther King, Jr. Dr. - App No. 23135

enrichment.relevance_reason: The rezoning would change a vacant lot from a residential district (RM-5) to a commercial district (B3-3), removing residentially zoned land, though no dwelling units are proposed.
enrichment.summary: BDT, Ltd. Holdings seeks to rezone the vacant 9,380 sq ft lot at 3927-33 S. King Drive from RM-5 to B3-3 to build a 30-foot restaurant building with zero dwelling units and no parking.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 12-K at 5312 S Kenneth Ave - App No. 23172

enrichment.relevance_reason: A rezoning of an existing multi-unit residential building from RS-2 to RT-4 bears on how residential property is zoned.
enrichment.summary: Midway 5312 S. Kenneth Avenue Condominium, represented by attorney Mark Kupiec, seeks to rezone 5312 S. Kenneth Ave from RS-2 to RT-4 to unify the lot under one zoning district. The existing building was built contrary to approved plans; the proposal is 3 dwelling units, no parking.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 3-I at 1140 N California Ave - App No. 23162T1

enrichment.relevance_reason: The rezoning from B3-1 to B3-3 is for a commercial and medical behavioral health clinic with no dwelling units, so it does not add or remove homes.
enrichment.summary: Humboldt Park Health seeks to rezone 1140 N. California Ave. from B3-1 to B3-3 Community Shopping District to build a 3-story outpatient behavioral health clinic, urgent care center, and medical office. It also seeks a 100% parking reduction.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 13-L at 4841 N Lipps Ave- App No. 23163

enrichment.relevance_reason: The rezoning would allow renovation of an existing mixed-use building to contain four dwelling units above a ground-floor commercial space.
enrichment.summary: 4841 Lipps LLC (Tim Pomaville) seeks to rezone 4841 N Lipps Ave from B3-2 to C1-2 to renovate an existing two-story mixed-use building into one ground-floor commercial space and four dwelling units. The 45th Ward alderman has no objection.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 12-D at 5482 S Ridgewood Ct - App No. 23170T1

enrichment.relevance_reason: A residential rezoning from RT-4 to RM-4.5 for a single-family home with a rear addition, which is a zoning map change affecting a residential lot.
enrichment.summary: Applicants Nabil M. Abou Baker and Sara G. Jelinek seek to rezone 5482 S Ridgewood Ct from RT-4 to RM-4.5 to replace a two-story rear addition on their single-family home, with setback and yard variations. No parking is provided.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 2-K at 4125 and 4127 W 5th Ave - App No. 23171T1

enrichment.relevance_reason: A rezoning from RT-4 to RM-4.5 would allow construction of two new three-unit residential buildings on vacant lots.
enrichment.summary: Techco Savvy Inc. seeks to rezone 4125 and 4127 W 5th Ave from RT-4 to RM-4.5 to split the lot and build two three-story buildings with three dwelling units each, plus setback variations.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 4-H at 2142 W 18th Pl - App No. 23173T1

enrichment.relevance_reason: The rezoning from RT-4 to RM-5 at a lot with five existing dwelling units would split the lot and allow a new three-unit residential building on the vacant parcel.
enrichment.summary: Coach House Properties LLC seeks to rezone 2142 W 18th Pl from RT-4 to RM-5 to split the lot in two. The existing five-unit building would remain, and a three-unit building would be built on the vacant lot, which stays RT-4.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 7-H at 2315-2317 W Barry Ave - App No. 23169T1

enrichment.relevance_reason: A rezoning from RS-3 (detached house) to RT-4 (two-flat, townhouse and multi-unit) changes the residential density allowed on the site.
enrichment.summary: Ordinance would rezone 2315-17 West Barry Avenue from RS-3 Residential Single-Unit (Detached House) to RT-4 Residential Two-Flat, Townhouse and Multi-Unit. The applicant is ZSD Barry LLC, per the attached Economic Disclosure Statements; no unit count is stated.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 5-H at 1933 N Winchester Ave - App No. 23175T1

enrichment.relevance_reason: A rezoning from RS-3 to RM-4.5 would legalize the fifth existing dwelling unit in a residential building.
enrichment.summary: Theus Property Holdings - 1933 N. Winchester L.L.C. seeks to rezone 1933 N. Winchester Ave from RS-3 to RM-4.5 to bring an existing fifth unit and a dormer into conformance. No expansion is proposed, and the ARO does not apply.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 15-J at 3244-3250 W Bryn Mawr Ave - App No. 23176T1

enrichment.relevance_reason: The Type 1 map amendment would let a vacant commercial building be redeveloped into a mixed-use building with 40 residential units and is subject to the ARO.
enrichment.summary: 3244-50 Bryn Mawr LLC asks to amend a previously approved Type 1 B2-3 map amendment at 3244-50 W Bryn Mawr Ave to allow a five-story building with 40 homes (up from 30) and 1,490 sq. ft. of ground-floor commercial space. It seeks reduced rear setback, lot area per unit and loading berth relief, and the project is subject to the ARO.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 18-E at 7353-7359 S Indiana Ave - App No. 23148T1

enrichment.relevance_reason: The rezoning from RS2 to RT4 would allow a new 8-unit residential building on a vacant lot.
enrichment.summary: 73RD AND INDIANA, LLC seeks a Type 1 rezoning of a vacant lot at 7353-59 S Indiana Ave from RS2 to RT4 to build a two-story, 8-unit residential building with a 7-car garage. The application states the project is not subject to the ARO.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 1-H at 2156 W Warren Blvd - App No. 23147T1

enrichment.relevance_reason: The rezoning would allow a new 8-unit residential building on a vacant lot, adding homes.
enrichment.summary: 2156 W Warren LLC seeks to rezone 2156 W Warren Blvd from RT4 to RM5 to build a new 4-story residential building with 8 dwelling units and 5 parking spaces on a vacant lot. The application says the project is not subject to the ARO.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 2-I at 2400 W Grenshaw St a.k.a. 1124 S Western Ave - App No. 23149T1

enrichment.relevance_reason: The rezoning from C1-2 to B2-3 would allow a new 4-story, 7-unit residential building, including ground-floor residential use, on a vacant lot.
enrichment.summary: The applicant seeks a Type 1 rezoning of 2400 W. Grenshaw St. from C1-2 Neighborhood Commercial to B2-3 Neighborhood Mixed-Use, with a rear setback variation, to build a 4-story, 7-unit residential building with 3 garage parking spaces on a vacant lot.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 8-G at 3439 S Morgan St - App No. 23152T1

enrichment.relevance_reason: The rezoning would allow a new six-unit residential building on a vacant lot in the 11th Ward.

enrichment.relevance_reason: The hearing covers a substantial amendment to the state's 2026 Action Plan for the federal Housing Trust Fund, which finances affordable housing.

notices.title: Presentations under the Municipal Advisor Registration Rules

enrichment.relevance_reason: This is an administrative notice about IHDA's independent registered municipal advisor exemption for financial firms, with no specific housing, financing deal, or tenant impact.
enrichment.summary: IHDA posted a notice that financial firms may use the SEC's independent registered municipal advisor exemption when advising it. IHDA says it relies on Caine Mitter & Associates Incorporated for advice on municipal financial products and securities issuance.

notices.title: Pheasant Ridge Hunter Apartments – October 15, 2026 at 10:00 a.m.

enrichment.relevance_reason: This is a TEFRA public hearing on IHDA tax-exempt bonds to finance acquisition, construction, or rehabilitation of a 176-unit multifamily apartment development.
enrichment.summary: IHDA will hold a hearing on October 15, 2026 on tax-exempt bonds of up to $51,500,000 for Pheasant Ridge/Hunter Apartments, a 176-unit multifamily property in Orland Hills. The owner is Standard PRHA Venture LP.

notices.title: Revenue Bonds 2026 Series LMNO – October 15, 2026 at 10:30 a.m.

enrichment.relevance_reason: The hearing covers IHDA's proposed issuance of up to $500 million in mortgage revenue bonds to finance home mortgage loans and down payment assistance in Illinois.
enrichment.summary: IHDA will hold a TEFRA public hearing on October 15, 2026 on issuing up to $500,000,000 in mortgage revenue bonds (2026 Series LMNO) over three years. Proceeds would finance qualifying mortgage loans, down payment and closing cost assistance, and refund prior bonds.

notices.title: Public Notice on IHDA’s Draft 2027-2028 Qualified Allocation Plan – English – Spanish

enrichment.relevance_reason: The Qualified Allocation Plan sets how Illinois awards Low-Income Housing Tax Credits for affordable housing development.
enrichment.summary: IHDA released its draft 2027-2028 Low-Income Housing Tax Credit Qualified Allocation Plan for public comment. A hybrid public hearing is set for June 8, 2026, and written comments are due by 5:00 P.M. on June 15, 2026.
